title: fix: isolate rolling metrics across setting changes
body:
## Summary

- Version each rolling measurement window and discard capture/inference results that finish after a reset.
- Reset the window when question selection or the custom prompt changes; manual reset also invalidates in-flight samples.
- Add six deterministic regression tests in `test/runner.test.mjs`, using the existing Node test runner and TypeScript dependency. No new dependencies or workflow changes.

## Why

Most experiment controls clear the rolling stats, but an inference that started before the reset can still finish afterward and repopulate the new window. Question toggles and custom-prompt edits also did not reset the window at all.

The invariant is: work admitted under an earlier measurement version cannot publish a sample, record telemetry, or commit a motion reference into the new window. The next valid sample must still be accepted without restarting the runner.

## Validation

The tests execute the production `LiveRunner`, with manually released capture, fetch, and response-body promises. Animation frames are explicitly advanced; there are no camera/model calls or timing-based sleeps.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Six existing protocol tests + six new runner tests (`node --test`) | 12 passed |
| New tests against the original runner at `ea031c7` | 4 failed, 2 unchanged-window controls passed |
| Remove only the post-capture version guard | Capture-reset regression fails |
| Remove only the post-response version guard | Response, response-body, and repeated-reset regressions fail |
| Syntax and whitespace checks on the added test | Passed |

Coverage includes reset during capture, while waiting for the response, and while decoding its body; repeated resets after an accepted sample; subsequent valid sampling; recording/motion-reference exclusion; and unchanged behavior with or without the optional version callback.

Local environment: Linux, Node **22.16.0**, preinstalled TypeScript **5.8.3**. The repository declares TypeScript `~5.9.3`; dependency downloads are unavailable in this sandbox, so **full `pnpm check` has not been run locally**. The runner and existing protocol sources used locally were verified against their Git blob SHAs. No browser DOM/event-wiring, camera, or model validation is claimed.

The test-only follow-up is `c590254`. [Upstream CI run 5](https://github.com/yoheinakajima/glance-speedlab/actions/runs/35948184442) currently reports `action_required`, not a passing check.

## Scope

This is a measurement-correctness fix, not a performance experiment. No changes to model scoring, request protocol, backend cancellation, or temporal-reuse policy; no latency improvement is claimed.

title: fix: distinguish result rate from processing rate
body:
## Summary

The live UI currently labels `1,000 / mean(loopMs)` as throughput in FPS. That describes processing time, but excludes scheduling gaps, retries, pauses, and temporal reuse between completed results.

This keeps that calculation as **processing rate** and shows a separate **result rate**, using monotonic completion timestamps retained alongside each sample. No new dependencies, timers, scheduler changes, or telemetry fields.

For example, two 100 ms inferences completing one second apart have **10 Hz processing rate but 1 Hz result rate**. This is a deterministic arithmetic example, not a measured model speedup.

Result rate uses `(N - 1) * 1,000 / (lastCompletionMs - firstCompletionMs)`: N retained completions define N−1 intervals. Before two completions, or for a zero-length interval, the display is `—`. Eviction and reset remove the corresponding timestamps too.

The UI note and architecture documentation make the boundary explicit: this is a completed-interval snapshot, updated on completion, not an instantaneous rate or observation age. Identical answers and cache hits still count as completed samples; multiple questions do not multiply the count.

Separate from #1: that PR prevents obsolete work from entering a new window; this PR distinguishes what the rates within a window mean. This branch is based directly on `ea031c7`, not stacked on #1.

## Evidence

- Experiment ID: not applicable; measurement-correctness change, with no performance-improvement claim.
- Primary check: waits between completions affect result rate without changing reciprocal-loop processing rate.
- Guardrail: existing latency summaries and model-timing semantics remain unchanged; model scoring, capture, scheduling, and recording schemas are untouched.
- Deterministic fixtures: nine new tests in `test/metrics.test.mjs`, exercising the production module with the existing TypeScript dependency.
- Local environment: Linux, Node 22.16.0, TypeScript 5.8.3. No camera or model run.

| Executed check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --test` | 15/15 pass: six existing protocol tests + nine metrics tests |
| Strict targeted type check of `metrics.ts` and `types.ts` | Pass |
| Substitute processing rate for result rate | Four tests fail |
| Count N rather than N−1 intervals | Five tests fail |
| Use calendar time instead of the monotonic clock | One test fails |
| In-memory Chromium DOM smoke | Eight display/reset states pass; camera, runner, network and clock mocked; no CSS/layout validation |

The published blobs were checked against the locally tested files. The sandbox cannot download the pinned dependencies, so full `pnpm check` and the Vite build have **not** been run. Local TypeScript 5.8.3 differs from the declared `~5.9.3`; upstream CI is still required.

## Checks

- [ ] `pnpm check`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] No camera frames, credentials, model weights, personal paths, or raw identifying data committed
- [x] Documentation and interpretation updated

title: feat: show displayed answer age from browser frame sampling
body:
## Summary

Show how long ago the displayed answer's supporting frame was sampled in the browser. The timestamp is taken immediately before the canvas draw, not after JPEG encoding or inference. A result that has just arrived can already be old.

This patch is based on `ea031c71355f85f1125bcdf3a15cd8d8c02c9876`, independently of #1 and #2. #1 isolates measurement windows; #2 distinguishes processing and result rates; this measures the age of the currently displayed observation.

- Carry the browser monotonic frame timestamp through the accepted sample, without sending it to the gateway or recording it in JSONL.
- Refresh the age every 250 ms while active. Reuse, pending work, and failed requests leave the existing answer aging.
- Keep that age when statistics reset. Clear the answer, timestamp, and display interval on stop or pagehide; restart stays unknown until another result is accepted.
- Document that browser frame-sampling age is not sensor age, source-frame liveness, answer correctness, or a hard refresh deadline.

No new dependencies, backend/scoring changes, inference scheduling changes, or request/recording schema changes. Temporal-reuse thresholds and refresh policy are untouched. No speedup is claimed; display-update overhead has not been measured.

## Validation

| Executed check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --test` | 19/19 pass: six existing protocol tests and 13 new answer-age tests |
| Strict targeted type check of the live camera/runner/UI/metrics/types modules | Pass |
| Seven deliberately broken variants | Every variant causes relevant tests to fail |
| Controlled Chromium checks | 15 pass; no page errors |
| Patch applied to a clean, verified source snapshot | All six resulting file hashes match the tested files; 19 tests and targeted type check pass again |
| `git diff --check` | Pass |

The unit tests execute the production modules using the existing TypeScript dependency. They use isolated DOM/clock/network doubles and controlled promises rather than a camera or model. The capture test distinguishes canvas-setup time, draw time, JPEG completion, and base64 completion. The runner tests cover delayed body consumption, rejection, stop, and timestamp exclusion from requests and metric beacons. UI tests cover reuse, stalled work, resets, stop/restart/pagehide, empty results, and unknown timestamps.

Mutation checks catch timestamping after JPEG, timestamping at response completion, transmitting the timestamp, using calendar time, resetting answer age with statistics, leaking the display timer, and refreshing the timestamp on each timer tick.

Local environment: Linux, Node 22.16.0, TypeScript 5.8.3, Chromium 144.0.7559.96. Chromium executed the production camera, runner, metrics and main modules in an in-memory page, with real DOM, canvas JPEG encoding and FileReader. Video/media, fetch responses, clock and scheduled callbacks were controlled; CSS was not loaded. This is not real-camera, model, layout, or performance validation.

## Still outstanding

- [ ] Full `pnpm check` with the pinned dependencies (`typescript ~5.9.3`); dependency downloads are unavailable in this sandbox.
- [ ] Real-camera/model validation and normal browser-layout inspection.
- [ ] Measurement of display-update overhead before using the instrumented UI for performance comparisons.

Keep this as a draft while the full build and live validation are outstanding. No reviewer request is needed yet.

This pull request does not replace #3; it is the same feature replayed on today's main so it can be reviewed against the merged measurement-window and rate work. Show how long ago the displayed answer's supporting frame was sampled in the browser. The timestamp is taken immediately before the canvas draw, not after JPEG encoding or inference. Combined behavior checked by reading the merge: - `measurementVersion` still discards in-flight captures and responses, so a settings change does not publish a stale sample or refresh answer age from discarded work. - Result rate and processing rate labels, metrics, and docs from #2 stay in place. - Resetting the measurement window still clears rolling statistics only. The displayed answer and its `capturedAt` age remain until a newly accepted result replaces them, or until stop/pagehide. - `capturedAt` is still stripped from the `/api/decide` client payload (`capturedAt: undefined` before `JSON.stringify`) and is not included in the metrics beacon body. ## Evidence - Experiment ID, if performance-related: none. No speedup is claimed, and display-update overhead has not been measured. - Primary metric: none (answer age is observational). - Quality guardrail: request and recorded telemetry schemas unchanged; age stays attached to the displayed answer across measurement resets. - Hardware, Glance commit, and model revision: not applicable; unit tests do not call a model. - Aggregate artifact: none. ## Checks - [x] `pnpm check` (34/34 tests, docs, `tsc --noEmit`, Vite build) on Node 22.14.0 / TypeScript 5.9.3 - [x] `git diff --check` - [x] No camera frames, credentials, model weights, personal paths, or raw identifying data committed - [x] Documentation and interpretation updated ## Still outstanding - Real-camera and model validation, and normal browser-layout inspection. - Measurement of display-update overhead before using the instrumented UI for performance comparisons. Original validation notes from #3 (Linux, Node 22.16.0, TypeScript 5.8.3, controlled Chromium doubles) still apply to the feature itself. This rebase re-runs the repository check on current main.
